summary: The Quest for El Dorado is a deck-building race game where players build a deck of movement cards to traverse a modular jungle path as fast as possible. It's approachable and quick, blending deck-building strategy with a straightforward race to the finish.
praised: Very approachable entry point into deck-building for newer gamers
Good variable routes and modular board keep it fresh
criticised: Less strategic depth than heavier deck-builders
Can feel like a solitaire race with limited direct interaction
Card draw luck affects a given turn's options
Some find repeated plays get a bit samey

interaction.kind: mostly parallel racing with light blocking
interaction.detail: Players race along a shared modular board and can occasionally block a path space or contest a shortcut, but each player's deck and hand are entirely their own. The main shared element is the board itself and the race positions on it.

scoring.why: There is no scoring at all — the game ends the instant a player's pawn crosses the finish line.
scoring.how_you_win: Build and upgrade your expedition deck with helpers and equipment so you can move efficiently through the jungle; the first player to get their pawn across the golden border wins outright.
